rationale: All three required findings are explicitly and correctly captured: humidity-gated sensor drift as a contributor (C2/C3/C6), the firmware retry defect as a contributor (C4/C7), and the conjunctive-necessity finding that neither alone sufficed, directly grounded in the comparison-run evidence (C5, CF1, CF2 using E6/E7). None of the three forbidden claims appear; the analysis explicitly denies single-factor sufficiency and explicitly denies that alert suppression initiated the breach (C9, CF4), correctly reframing suppression as an exposure-duration effect rather than a causal trigger. Causal structure is represented with correct direction (drift/defect -> conjunction -> breach; suppression -> extended exposure, downstream of breach) and interaction is modeled explicitly as a conjunction rather than additive or single-cause. The one moderately speculative link (C6->C7 'mediates') is appropriately flagged at low confidence rather than asserted, so it doesn't constitute invented structure being passed off as established. Evidence discipline is strong: claims map to specific evidence IDs, confidence levels are calibrated to evidentiary directness (high for E1-based/comparison-supported claims, medium/low for inferential mechanism claims), and no outside-evidence claims are introduced. Uncertainty handling is thorough and well-targeted (magnitude/severity unknown, timeout trigger unresolved, comparison-run equivalence unverified, control-vs-display corruption unresolved), preserving live alternatives (e.g., a shared upstream cause of timeouts) rather than hiding them. Actions correctly prioritize the two conjunction-breaking interventions (A1, A2) as high leverage, correctly demote the alerting fix to medium/secondary leverage matching the ground-truth preferred action, and propose no harmful or control-weakening actions. This is a well-calibrated, evidence-disciplined analysis with no material errors against the rubric.
